board:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: a clean, flat museum information-board texture for a 3D reconstruction of Gaziantep Panorama 25 Aralik Museum.
Input 1 is the edit target: the user's screenshot of the blurry board. Input 2 is the original panoramic photograph containing that same board, left of the central column. Input 3 is another original photograph showing the board below the balcony, left of the stairs.
Extract ONLY the actual dark information board from its surrounding wall and frame, rectify it to a perfectly front-facing flat rectangle, and restore contrast and edge clarity. Output a landscape 4:3 texture filling the entire image, with no perspective, surrounding wall, ceiling, cursor, shadows, glare, reflections, or 3D frame.
Preserve the museum's actual board composition: dark warm charcoal background with the subtle archival map motif; the red Turkish heading "Haritada Gösterilen Yerler" at upper left; the small yellow English subtitle as in the original; the narrow white numbered place-name columns; the red "Harita Kaynakları" heading and white source-text blocks on the right; the red/white Panorama 25 Aralik logo at lower left. Preserve column count, row order, and alignment.
Accuracy is essential. Do not invent any place name, date, map source, or number. Recover body lettering only when supported by the references; for genuinely unrecoverable fine lettering, retain faithful subdued source detail rather than replacing it with fabricated plausible words. Do not add decorations or any new text. A restoration of this exact board, not a new museum sign. High-resolution, crisp print texture.
map:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: a flat overhead historical floor-map texture for the Gaziantep Panorama 25 Aralik Museum, for mapping onto a 3D floor.
The four input photographs are overlapping original views of the SAME map painted/printed on the museum floor. Recover the map artwork from these views into ONE coherent, clean, top-down orthographic map. Use image 2 (IMG_1976) as the main layout/orientation reference, and images 1, 3 and 4 to corroborate matching features.
Remove all museum architecture, columns, people, reflections, glare, ceiling, lighting, tile glare, and perspective distortion. Deliver only the flat map artwork, square composition, suitable as an opaque albedo texture. Preserve the visible historic Antep city layout: dense irregular terracotta/orange urban blocks with fine dark street outlines; the recognizable fortified castle mound in its green enclosure; the winding blue/turquoise stream that curves around that area; olive-green open land, brown terrain, broad dusty-rose route bands, and the red dashed route visible in the sources. Keep their relationships and course faithful to the same source map. Do not turn it into a modern generic city or add fictional monuments/streets.
Preserve only clearly readable authentic labels and marks. Do not invent readable historical names, dates or cartographic facts. Use restrained neutral continuation at genuinely unobserved outer margins instead of inventing new city detail. Keep the museum map's existing hand-rendered cartographic/terrain appearance, clear fine lines and printed colors, without a border, title card, legend panel or decorative elements. High resolution and uniform matte lighting.
